scenes.title: Examiner's Margin — lesson overview
scenes.narration: Welcome to IELTS Winners. This lesson shows how to describe a household expenditure table in IELTS Academic Writing Task One. We compare Canada, Japan, Mexico, and Germany across housing, food, transport, and others. You'll identify key comparisons, write an effective overview, and structure a four-paragraph Band Eight response.

scenes.title: Step 1 — Analyse the table
scenes.narration: Step one: analyse the table using E R C S. Find extremes, rankings, comparisons, and spread. Japan records the highest overall figure: forty-eight percent for Others, but the lowest transport share at ten percent. Canada leads housing with twenty-eight percent, while Mexico leads food with twenty-four percent. Transport varies least.

scenes.title: Step 2 — Four-paragraph response
scenes.narration: Step two: write four paragraphs. Paraphrase the task, then give an overview without figures. Use body paragraph one to compare housing and food, and paragraph two for transport and others. Notice the model answer groups related figures and supports each comparison. The overview highlights patterns; the body paragraphs provide evidence.

scenes.title: Step 3 — Language toolkit
scenes.narration: Step three: upgrade your language. Forty-eight percent is nearly half; twenty-eight percent is slightly over a quarter; twenty-four percent is almost a quarter; twenty percent is one fifth; and ten percent is one tenth. Try account for, represent, and make up. Connect comparisons with whereas, in contrast, and similarly.

scenes.title: Steps 4–7 — Group and refine
scenes.narration: Steps four to seven bring everything together. Group housing with food, then transport with others. Upgrade basic sentences: housing accounted for the largest share in Canada, at twenty-eight percent. Avoid listing every figure, repeating the introduction, or comparing without evidence. Finish with an introduction, overview, and two grouped detail paragraphs. Analyse, group, compare.
